questions.question: An open network of $M$ stations has Poisson external arrivals, Markov routing, $c_i$ exponential servers at station $i$ and every station stable. Which statement gives the stationary joint distribution $p(n_1,\ldots,n_M)$ of the station contents according to Jackson's theorem?
options: One geometric law in the total $n_1+\cdots+n_M$, with load $\sum_i\rho_i$
$\prod_i p_i(n_i)$, with $p_i$ the $M/M/c_i$ law at the traffic-equation rate $\lambda_i$
$\prod_i p_i(n_i)$, but only when every station has a single server
Marginals are $M/M/c_i$ laws, but the stations are dependent, so no product

questions.question: In an open Jackson network with external arrival rates $\gamma_i$, routing matrix $\boldsymbol{P}$ and single-server stations with mean service times $\mathbb{E}[S_i]$, which load $\rho_i$ enters the factor $p_i(n_i)=(1-\rho_i)\rho_i^{n_i}$ of station $i$?
options: $\rho_i=\gamma_i\mathbb{E}[S_i]$, with $\gamma_i$ the external arrival rate at station $i$
$\rho_i=|\boldsymbol{\gamma}|\mathbb{E}[S_i]$, with $|\boldsymbol{\gamma}|$ the total external arrival rate
$\rho_i=\lambda_i\mathbb{E}[S_i]$, with $\boldsymbol{\lambda}$ solving $\boldsymbol{\lambda}=\boldsymbol{\gamma}+\boldsymbol{\lambda}\boldsymbol{P}$
$\rho_i=\lambda_i/\mathbb{E}[S_i]$, with $\boldsymbol{\lambda}$ solving $\boldsymbol{\lambda}=\boldsymbol{\gamma}+\boldsymbol{\lambda}\boldsymbol{P}$

questions.question: In an open Jackson network, station $i$ has $c_i$ servers, mean service time $\mathbb{E}[S_i]$ and total arrival rate $\lambda_i$ from the traffic equations. Which condition on these quantities does Jackson's theorem require?
options: $\lambda_i\mathbb{E}[S_i]/c_i<1$ for every station $i=1,\ldots,M$
$\sum_{i=1}^M\lambda_i\mathbb{E}[S_i]/c_i<1$ for the network as a whole
$\lambda_i\mathbb{E}[S_i]/c_i<1$ only at stations with $\gamma_i>0$
$\frac{1}{M}\sum_{i=1}^M\lambda_i\mathbb{E}[S_i]/c_i<1$, the average load

questions.question: Jackson's theorem assumes Markov routing with routing matrix $\boldsymbol{P}=(p_{ij})$. What does this assumption say about a job that has just finished service at station $i$?
options: It follows a fixed route through the stations that was assigned when it entered
It joins the station $j$ with the fewest jobs, using $p_{ij}$ only to break ties
It goes to station $j$ with probability $p_{ij}$ but never revisits a station
It goes to station $j$ with probability $p_{ij}$, independently of its past route

questions.question: In an open Jackson network with feedback, a job may return to a station it has visited before. What holds for the total arrival stream into such a station and for the product form?
options: The stream is Poisson with rate $\lambda_i$, and this is why the product form holds
The stream is in general not Poisson, yet the product form still holds
The stream is in general not Poisson, so the product form fails here
The stream is Poisson with rate $\gamma_i$, as fed-back jobs are not arrivals

questions.question: Jobs arrive as a Poisson process with rate $\lambda=1$ per hour at station 1 of a tandem of two exponential single-server stations, with mean service times $\mathbb{E}[S_1]=0.6$ and $\mathbb{E}[S_2]=0.5$ hours. What is the stationary probability $\mathbb{P}(L_1>2)$ that station 1 holds more than two jobs?

An open Jackson network has three single-server stations with loads $\rho_1=0.5$, $\rho_2=0.6$ and $\rho_3=0.8$ (each $\rho_i=\lambda_i\mathbb{E}[S_i]$ from the traffic equations). What is the stationary probability that the whole network is empty?

In a stationary Jackson tandem line, Poisson jobs (rate $\lambda=1$ per hour) are served at exponential station 1 (mean $0.5$ hours) and then at exponential station 2 (mean $0.4$ hours) before leaving. What is the probability $p(1,2)$ of one job at station 1 and two at station 2?

An open Jackson network has two single-server stations with loads $\rho_1=0.5$ and $\rho_2=0.75$, computed from the traffic equations. What is the stationary expected total number of jobs $\mathbb{E}[L]$ in the network?

In an open Jackson network, station 2 has $c_2=2$ exponential servers, total arrival rate $\lambda_2=3$ per hour (from the traffic equations) and mean service time $\mathbb{E}[S_2]=0.5$ hours. Which statement about the factor $p_2$ of the product form is correct?
options: Station 2 is unstable since $3\cdot0.5=1.5\ge1$, so no product form exists
$p_2(n)=0.25\cdot0.75^{n}$, an $M/M/1$ law with load $0.75$
$p_2$ is the product of two $M/M/1$ laws, each with arrival rate $1.5$
$p_2$ is the $M/M/2$ stationary law with rate $3$ and load per server $0.75$

questions.question: Two single-server stations in tandem form a Jackson network: jobs arrive at station 1 as a Poisson process with rate $\lambda$ per hour, go to station 2 after service, and leave after service there; service times are exponential and independent. Assume $\lambda<1/\mathbb{E}[S_1]$ and $\lambda<1/\mathbb{E}[S_2]$. Why may station 2 be analysed as an $M/M/1$ queue with arrival rate $\lambda$?
options: The departures of a stationary $M/M/1$ queue form a Poisson process with rate $\lambda$
The departures of station 1 form a Poisson process with rate $\mu_1=1/\mathbb{E}[S_1]$
The times between departures at station 1 equal its exponential service times
The stream into station 2 is Poisson because station 2 itself is stable

questions.question: Two single-server stations are placed in tandem with Poisson arrivals at station 1. Station 1 has deterministic service times and station 2 has exponential service times; both loads $\rho_1$ and $\rho_2$ are below one. Which statement about the stationary joint distribution of $(L_1,L_2)$ is correct?
options: It is a product form with an $M/G/1$ factor for station 1 and an $M/M/1$ factor for station 2
It is not a product form, but each marginal keeps the geometric law $(1-\rho_i)\rho_i^{n}$ of an $M/M/1$ queue
No product form is guaranteed, because Jackson's theorem needs exponential service at both stations
It is a product form, because the departures of station 1 are still a Poisson process with rate $\lambda$

questions.question: In a tandem of two exponential single-server stations with Poisson arrivals at rate $\lambda$ at station 1, write $\mu_1$ and $\mu_2$ for the service rates and $(i,j)$ for $i$ jobs at station 1 and $j$ at station 2. For an interior state with $i,j\ge1$, from which states and at which rates does the chain enter $(i,j)$?
options: $(i-1,j)$ at rate $\lambda$, $(i-1,j+1)$ at rate $\mu_1$, $(i,j+1)$ at rate $\mu_2$
$(i-1,j)$ at rate $\lambda$, $(i+1,j-1)$ at rate $\mu_1$, $(i,j+1)$ at rate $\mu_2$
$(i-1,j)$ at rate $\lambda$, $(i+1,j-1)$ at rate $\mu_1$, $(i,j-1)$ at rate $\mu_2$
$(i+1,j)$ at rate $\lambda$, $(i-1,j+1)$ at rate $\mu_1$, $(i,j-1)$ at rate $\mu_2$

questions.question: Two exponential single-server stations in tandem form a Jackson network: jobs arrive at station 1 as a Poisson process with rate $\lambda=1$ per hour, the service rates are $\mu_1=2$ and $\mu_2=4$ per hour, and $p(i,j)$ denotes the stationary probability of $i$ jobs at station 1 and $j$ at station 2. Given $p(0,0)=\tfrac{3}{8}$, which value of $p(0,1)$ does the balance equation of the empty state $(0,0)$ give?

An open Jackson network of three single-server stations receives external jobs at total rate $|\boldsymbol{\gamma}|=2$ per hour. The traffic equations give $\boldsymbol{\lambda}=(2,4,3)$ and the loads are $\boldsymbol{\rho}=(0.5,0.8,0.6)$. What is the expected sojourn time $\mathbb{E}[J]$ of a job in the network?
options: $\mathbb{E}[J]\approx0.72$ hours
$\mathbb{E}[J]=6.5$ hours
$\mathbb{E}[J]=3.25$ hours
$\mathbb{E}[J]=2.0$ hours

questions.question: An open Jackson network has two single-server stations with total arrival rates $\lambda_1=4$ and $\lambda_2=2$ per hour (from the traffic equations) and mean service times $\mathbb{E}[S_1]=0.15$ and $\mathbb{E}[S_2]=0.4$ hours. What is the stationary probability that exactly one of the two stations is empty?

Two stationary $M/M/1$ stations in tandem form a Jackson network with loads $\rho_1=0.9$ and $\rho_2=0.5$. At time $t$ station 1 is seen to hold $20$ jobs. Which statement about the number of jobs $L_2$ at station 2 is correct?
options: At time $t$, $L_2$ is likely larger than usual, since the stations are dependent at a fixed moment
At time $t$ and at all later times, $L_2$ keeps the law $(1-\rho_2)\rho_2^{n}$, by independence
At time $t$, $L_2$ is likely smaller than usual, since station 1 is holding back the jobs
At time $t$, $L_2$ has law $(1-\rho_2)\rho_2^{n}$, but shortly after its mean exceeds $\mathbb{E}[L_2]$

questions.question: For an open Jackson network with feedback routes, which argument establishes that $p(n_1,\ldots,n_M)=\prod_i p_i(n_i)$ is the stationary distribution of the station contents?
options: Show that each station's total arrival stream is Poisson with rate $\lambda_i$, then treat the stations separately
Substitute $\prod_i p_i(n_i)$ into the balance equations of the joint process and check every state
Show that the departure streams of all stations are mutually independent Poisson processes
Solve the balance equations of each station in isolation; independence then follows automatically

questions.question: A single exponential server receives external Poisson arrivals at rate $\gamma=3$ per hour and has mean service time $\mathbb{E}[S]=0.25$ hours. After each service the job returns to the same station with probability $p$ and otherwise leaves, independently. For which $p$ does the Jackson network have a stationary distribution?
options: $0\le p<\tfrac{1}{4}$
$0\le p<\tfrac{1}{3}$
$0\le p\le\tfrac{1}{4}$

questions.question: A tandem line has two exponential single-server stations, a Poisson arrival rate $\lambda=1$ per hour at station 1, and mean service times of $0.5$ hours at station 1 and $0.2$ hours at station 2. At a stationary moment the line is seen to hold exactly one job in total. What is the probability that this job is at station 2, $\mathbb{P}(L_2=1\mid L_1+L_2=1)$?
